reviews.comment: Honestly could not have asked for a better professor. She taught the material amazingly. Only issue, this was her 1st time teaching this class & first exam was incredibly hard to finish on time. Focused on one kind of problem with multiple ways of solving it. Not an impossible class just lots of effort needed compared to past cals.
Going to the lectures helped me prepare for the homework, quizzes helped prepare for tests.

Professor Sengupta made lectures engaging and 151 very understandable. Because the exams are common, there are a ton of practice exams and resources. She drops the last few quizzes and the final can replace your lowest midterm. As long as you take the time to study, you will do well in this class. Take Sengupta if you can!!

Professor Sengupta was a great Differential Equations professor. Her lectures were organized, clear, and easy to follow, and she explained difficult concepts in a way that made them much easier to understand. She genuinely cared about student learning and created a positive environment in class. I learned a lot and would definitely recommend her.
Amazing teacher, very considerate, asks for reviews on her exams to make sure we think they are fair. Made this class 100 times easier than it would be with any other professor.

She subbed for my previous Calc 3 prof for a large chunk of the semester and did a great job taking over lectures. She made the sudden transition feel a lot easier with her teaching style. She always checked to make sure we followed her explanations. Very receptive to feedback and responded to emails quickly. Overall one of the best math profs.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very good prof for differential equations. Very thorough, at times frustrating when she tries cramming a lot at the end of lecture, but nothing unmanageable. Great handwriting, completed notes were posted for us, and you can tell she tries her best to be caring and thoughtful of us college students. would recommend.
I took Calc 1 in high school so that definitely helped going into MATH 151. However, Prof Sengupta made the lectures very easy to understand and gave lots of material to practice.

Many students who take 151 usually have taken Calc 1 before, but her lectures are extremely easy to understand. Her notes and lectures are available after the lecture. I do feel like she teaches topics more slowly than other professors, but she makes videos and posts them when she doesn't finish them in class.

She is a great professor. Though a lot of her students have already taken calc 1 before she ensures she teaches it to where someone who has never taken a calculus class before can understand it very well. People say she rushes at the end of class, but she always goes back over what she "rushed" next class. Amazing professor and person
Super nice professor, if your struggling she will really help you out if you reach out to her and her notes and stuff is really accessible
Prof Sengupta is really nice and her lectures are clear. Just keep up with the material and do practice exams.

Great professor if you have already taken Calc AB / BC! She is very thorough in what exactly you need to know, and she is always accessible outside of class. The exams and final were very multiple-choice heavy, and taking a few practice tests should be more than enough to prepare you for each test.

She replaced my previous MATH 251 professor while simultaneously teaching MATH 151 which likely contributed to delayed grading which was understandable. However, she often assumed prior knowledge, and explanations were unclear, making the material difficult to follow. The hardest part of the class is the material taught two weeks before the final.

This class was just an easy review of Calc AB. The lectures are fine and informative, but you could probably get away with not going if you've already taken calc. For exams, just do as many previous exams as possible and you'll be fine. The final was incredibly easy and all multiple choice. Nothing too difficult, just do the work and study.

Math 151 is a common exam course and the previous exams really helped with studying. The lectures were amazing and gave helpful information outside of math. The python labs were not too bad. Unfortunately they won't be posting any previous exams or lecture recordings next semester which is the sole reason I passed this class.

ok lecturer, some discrepancies between different methods that aren't clarified. she honestly has a condescending attitude towards questions and talking to her is just as bad. it's an easy class, mostly exam heavy! just dont expect her to help you very much, seek the MLC
Very sweet and lovely teacher who gives good lectures. The course is very exam-heavy but there is plenty of material given to study for it.

super sweet and was very accessible outside class. easy class overall and she was a very good teacher and explained things thoroughly and would do in class reviews before exams open for students to ask any questions.

Excellent professor with comforting personality. The course is pretty test heavy with 80% of the grade being made up of 3 tests and the final, but assignments are pretty easy (python assignments are pointless imo but that's not her fault). Lectures are well paced and she will take time before the test to answer questions and go over past exams.

Excellent professor! She takes the time to explain concepts very clearly and genuinely cares about her students. Seemed very accessible in office hours and even dropped several of our lowest grades towards the end of the semester. I would take her for every math course if I could!

Dr. Sengupta is an amazing teacher, her lectures are simplified so the concepts are easy to grasp. She is conversational, approachable and very friendly! I liked how she emphasized what need to know for the tests/going forward. I took Calc BC beforehand in hs btw.

Amazing professor, I had her at 8am so waking up was a hassle but she managed to make my mornings fun. Calculus in general is a bit difficult, but she was always open to questions and very easily accessible. She is more than happy to help you with whatever you need! 
Also, she was very kindhearted, and you can tell she cares about her students.

Had her over the summer for an engineering preparation program (she specifically helped us prepare for MATH 151). She is very sweet and caring, which was clear when she shared tips on staying healthy and surviving freshman year of college. Really cares for her students and took the time to get to know us (though bear in mind we were a small class).

I had her for her 8am section and I can count on one hand the amount of times she was on time, however, she always was high energy and made the content enjoyable. She is really sweet and makes it a point to recognize the people who come to class everyday and/or office hours.

Dr. Sengupta is very thorough in her lecture and takes a lot of time going through practice problems and answering questions, which is very helpful. She's super kind and just a great person all around.

She is great. The lectures are useful and she is a kind and understanding person. The python lab portion is a huge waste of time but overall she is a great professor. Make sure to do past common exams online. Do like 4 or 5 of them before a test and your very likely to do well.
Good lectures

Oh my gosh I love Dr. Sengupta so much she is so sweet! Her lectures are phenomenal and she always sends out videos of her lectures through email after class in case you miss. She is such a good professor I highly recommend!!

Absolute angel sent to earth. I took calc in high school and struggled really hard to understand the concepts and do well in the class. She teaches in a very clear and straight forward manner and explains well the conceptual and math aspects which makes it easier to understand. Lecture questions strongly resemble what is on the quizzes and exams
She's very sweet and caring. This was my second time taking the course and she explains very well.

She teaches in a clear and easy to understand way. She doesn't make the course more complicated than it needs to be. Drops two lowest hw and video quizzes, replaces lowest exam with final if higher, and reachable in office hours. Highly recommend her!!!

She is the best professor I've had so far. This class is really hard, but having a professor that actually cares and is willing to help you makes it better. I failed this class my first semester, but I retook it with her and finished with an A. Its not impossible!! Go to week in reviews and get extra help if you need it. Office hours very helpful.

Always willing to help when asked a question and always open to explaining things further. Does give a good chunk of homework but not incredibly demanding, always seemed ok with pushing back some homework deadlines if needed.
fav professor! she is so sweet and is willing to work with you to make sure you get everything!!

Math 151 is a common course so the difficulty isn't really on her, she does a great job explaining each subject but sometimes skips over a few questions but posts videos of them online. She posts tons of resources on canvas that help you with the exams and homework and she really cares about her students.

Posted all recorded lectures and notes online except for the last 2-3 weeks. No required attendance but go because the lectures are much better in person. Easy to understand and good at explaining, although sometimes the lectures were rushed, and some questions were skipped over to save time. I never went but I heard how good her office hours were.

Professor Sengupta was the best. She organized her lectures very well and made sure students kept up with the material. Attend lecture, recitation and office hours since she makes an effort to get to know her students and help them with everything they need. She also provides past exams to get a general idea of how questions will be structured.

Professor Sengupta is very dedicated to the class, explains concepts very well, and releases lecture videos with extra practice problems after class. Calculus confused me a lot when I first looked at it, but she made everything make much more sense than it has in the past. You definitely have to do the work, but if you do, you'll be in a good spot
Professor Sengupta explained each concept clearly and provided numerous additional materials to help students practice calculus.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: great prof

She is a really sweet lady, took the time to remember my name even though I really had not talked to her at all besides emailing her once for a sickness absence. She lectures pretty decently and makes sure that we actually understand what she is teaching and will change what she is doing based on that. I would take her again if I had to choose.

Loves to rush through lectures and if you ask to a question to clear up a confusion you might have, majority of time you will be met with attitude. She nice to talk to and gives candy for holidays, but teaching wise, super strict or comes off as rude.

Dr. Sengupta was my Calc 3 prof last semester, and she did an amazing job at it. Her lectures were very in depth. She frequently connected the concepts in class to real world concepts using her physics background. She was very kind and even gave us Oreos before spring break. Great prof!

Extremely well structured. Lectures are very comprehensive. Near exams lectures become more rushed, however online resources are available if there is any confusion. Overall the class is very fair, and the lectures are very good.
Great lectures!

3 Tests 1 Final are most of your grade
Review for each test given on Canvas at least a week before the exam
Speaks very clearly and will answer any questions before or after class
Online 2-question video quizzes are annoying and happen often just dont forget
group quizzes about once a week

From what I hear the best professor for 140

I took Calc 3 with her over the summer and she taught the first half. Lectures were so engaging and she covered the material phenomenally! She is also a nice and caring person! Homework and weekly quizzes were a pain, but that's not unusual for any Calc 3 section. Exams were very fair if you can do the homework by yourself!

Professor Sengupta is a great math teacher. Her lectures are clear, and she's happy to help during office hours. Using resources like unstuckstudy AI, practice exams, and Cengage homework helped me do well in this challenging course.
okay, so I posted the other one star by this. I messed up and meant to say choose the prof with the highest grade distribution.

TONS of homework and that is a small percentage of the grade, does not help much with the test-heavy class. Not a lot of good profs to choose from for this class and prof highest grade distribution. Beware said we should only have time to do her class. got annoyed when students didn't know everything even though she said she was open to questions.

Really nice lady. Lectures were generally clear. Tests were on the easier end compared to other profs but you still have to study for them. She struggled to manage her time as in tests take a WHILE to grade and lectures were rushed, especially during the last few units. To do WELL in this class use Joe Kahlig's website as a supplement.

Calc 3 is a very difficult class and Sengupta is a great professor. You have to put in the work, she will not give anything for free. Do practice exams and do your hw, it will help a lot. Office hours are also great. There's 3 exams and a final. The 3 midterms are 50 minutes long so make sure you work fast

Gives a lot of practice exams. Questions in test are of the same type as material covered in class and in cengage. You will have a lot of resources to train yourself. If you do the week in review, cengage hws by hand, and read the lecture notes for each test you will be golden. Make sure to not be lazy on any test.

Great at explaining the difficult concepts and extremely accessible and helpful during office hours. Her tests are extremely fair and mainly draw from the homework. She clearly cares about her students and always asks for feedback on what she could be doing better. Amazing prof.

Very good at explaining difficult concepts and willing to help if there is any confusion. Very fair grading system with exams similar to homework and practice quizzes. Not an easy class but Dr. Sengupta will make it as painless as possible.

She was better for calc 2 than calc 3, but still good. Her notes were long and often excessive, and she rushed a lot it felt like. She also recorded on zoom a lot which took away from the class feeling sometimes. Other than that, great prof who respects her students and is really funny at times. Definitely try to take her. She will hear feedback.

Amazing teacher and cares a lot about her students. Always eager to answer any questions students may have. Workload is reasonable and although some hw questions are tricky, help is easily accessible. Lectures and notes are easy to follow (her handwriting was oddly satisfying). Took her for math152 too and really liked her teaching style.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed being in her class. Dr. Sengupta is very helpful and cares about her students a lot. Although the material was difficult at times, she explained it really well and worked through many examples. I would definitely recommend for cal 3, or any math class at that.

Dr. Sengupta is one of the best professors in the math department. Her lectures are simple and easy to understand and she prepares her students well for the exams. She is also super helpful during office hours and easy to reach if you have any questions. Highly recommend!

She was a good teacher but struggled to manage her time. In the later units, some homework and concepts required multiple examples to fully grasp, and I feel as if sometimes she didn't do enough. Regardless, she still taught well and cared for her students so I would recommend her.

Sengupta is the worst Math professor I have had at Texas A&M. She constantly rushes during class and will skip problems entirely or only set them up. She does record lectures so that was nice considering how fast she goes in class. She was also very rude during her limited office hours which she would leave to go do other things.

Cal III is definitely harder than cal II despite what people might say. Sengupta is great but she definitely taught calc II a little better. Overall the class isn't that bad and the exams are fairly straight forward. Get used to being crunched for time during the exams as they go from 2 hours in cal II to 50 minutes in cal III.
A really good teacher who genuinely takes the time to explain the topics thoroughly. This is only a hard class because of the material but she makes it bearable!

Had her for both 251 and 152, fantastic professor for both. Super helpful and really cares about your success, problem is a lot of people don't put in the effort to keep up with how difficult her classes are. Super accessible and is there to help you, seek her out, its worth it.

Dr Sengupta is an amazing prof. Going in with only the AB credit, she makes calc 2 as digestible as possible. If you go to office hours and ask questions she will get to know your name and check in on you. She's not fake whatsoever, she puts in a lot of effort for her students and it shows. Taking her again for calc 3

Math has always been one of my least favorite subjects but Professor Sengupta made lecture really enjoyable. She teaches at a good pace in an easy to follow way and really cares to see her students succeed.  Overall one of the best math classes I have been in.

Dr. Sengupta makes MATH152, a difficult class, the easiest it can get. Her tests align directly with what is in lectured in class. It is clear that Dr. Sengupta wants her students to have a strong conceptual grasp of what is going on. Use the common exams to study for tests, and if there is a unit you're struggling with go to office hours, it helps

Professor Sengupta made a difficult class that much easier. Her lectures are thorough and she really takes the time to clear any doubts. Do the homework, ask questions, and practice for the exams and you will do fine.

Overall a good professor. She gave clear examples and made an effort to post her very detailed notes online as soon as possible. She made a difficult class easy to understand and was adamant about answering questions in class and after class. One of the best professors I've taken here. Do practice exams and attend lectures and you will do fine.
Sengussy is an engaging professor who just happens to teach a hard class. She genuinely cares about her students, is a great lecturer, and most of all she is fair.

Overall good professor. Due dates always clear and pushed some back when she knew we had exams for other courses. The class in itself sucks, regardless of what professor you take it with. Definitely a little stricter on engagement during class, but attendance not required. Class is test heavy with common exams being roughly 80% of the grade

Someone explain why she yelled at my class 3x during the semester about putting our phones away. By far worst explainer of math concepts I've ever encountered. Toughest grader possible on FRQs on common exams. Just run. Hated this class. M152 does not have to be this hard.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Dr. Sengupta was very clear in her lectures and has an easy-to-follow pace. All of her blank notes are uploaded early in canvas and all her assignments are very clear for due dates.
A majority of your grade will be through common exams (all sections take exam at same time) and she uploads previous exams and answer keys onto canvas. 
Very Kind.

She teaches so well and so clearly. She doesn't go fast so her lectures are easy to follow and very clear to understand. Exams are just like the practice tests she gave us. Homework are easy. Quizes are easy (although they only consists of 3-4 problems so if you mess up on one problem you lose like 1/3 of the points but they are easy though).
Calc II can be very hard for some students but Sengupta explains topics very well. The homework and practicing the previous common exams are the key to succeeding in this class.
Overall pretty good, doesn't really explain everything super well, had to ask for help in tutoring

Sengupta is one of the best professors I have studied under. She keeps her lectures to the point and her notes and homework correspond directly to what is asked on the exams. There are plenty of labs, quizzes, and homework so if you miss one, do not stress about it. She is patient and accessible outside the class. Overall, great professor.

Overall, an amazing teacher. Does a good job of answering questions and preparing you for homeworks and tests. Best thing to study for tests is the math 151 common exam archives. Almost the same questions just different wording here and there.

Professor Sengupta truly cares about her students. She is a great lecturer, and knows how to teach. She provides us with everything needed to succeed, replies to emails quickly, and has office hours regularly. Great proff, would highly recommend.

For those who are lucky enough to get her, she will be your angel for Calculus. Her lectures are so straightforward and easy to follow. She is understanding and is willing to help outside of class as well. She is also funny here and there as well. Definitely recommend and I would take her ANY year!!

I would highly take this class again with this prof. I had horrible time-management skills and ended up with my grade but her lectures were very well organized and she did an amazing job at explaining the concepts if you ever needed help outside of the class. She also did an amazing job teaching the Math-in-Review sessions during the last semester!

She taught the class well. She was available for office hours and took her time during lectures. She took questions during lectures and gave good feedback. When we got behind on material, she postponed homework due dates and changed what material was covered on quizzes.

She posts her notes and explains how to do the math really well. She's caring and more than willing to help if ur struggling. 2-3 topics of math homework per week and there's 3 tries per question, 4 tests total where the final can replace ur lowest grade if higher. Quizzes r 3 questions and math labs can be time consuming.

Dr Sengupta is very kind, caring, and good at teaching. I had taken AP Calc AB in High School so 151 wasn't very difficult at all, but Sengupta still explained things well and was funny every once and a while. Made a class GroupMe which was helpful, she is accessible if needed, put in the work, study hard, use the MLC even if you know the material
Wonderful professor. Tries to make the lecture fun, posts the lecture notes (plain and annotated), and provides note templates.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
love love love her. she was so great, lecturing was great, she was really patient and would always take questions, she would cancel class when we had a late exam the night before. would sometimes record lectures so was super accessible

hw was annoying sometimes but honestly was good practice, lab assgnmnts were a bit tedious but ta was helpful
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Sengupta is absolutely amazing. Came in with a background in calculus, but the concepts that I did not remember, she went over very well. Overall the HW is not difficult and the exams are very easy to study for using the Math 151 Common Exam Archive. There are weekly quizzes to reinforce topics taught in the week prior.
She started to do recordings outside of class as well. Great professor that is passionate about the subject. She will usually try to help you out as long as you go and ask.
She was so funny and sweet. My only complain is that she occasionally skips small steps when working out a problem. She makes math bearable.
Easy class when taken with Sengupta
Great professor, very funny and super accessible through groupme. She really cares about her students and lectures really well. Doesn't do lecture recordings, so don't skip class.

Sengupta is an outstanding professor. Her lectures are not only entertaining but very beneficial. She teaches very well and is easily accessible outside of class. If you have questions over the homework, do not hesitate to send an email or attend office hours. This course requires studying, but the resources are extremely helpful.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Sengupta is one of those professors that just makes the class so easy and fun to study. Tests are a breeze if you pay a modicum of attention during lecture and TAs are a help during lab periods. If I could I would take her again next semester for 152 but sadly she will not be teaching next semester.  :,(
Great professor and she made it easy to learn concepts. Class will be a breeze if you did well in high school calc.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor. Would take again
Fun professor, easy class if you took AP Calculus, go to class or else you may miss something easy that you never covered in high school

After taking this class I am genuinely worried that I will not have a professor I like more. Dr Sengupta is not only a great teacher but a great person. She is incredibly understanding when you do not understand and she responds to emails and Group Me incredibly fast. She is unironically funny and makes lectures interesting.

Dr. Sengupta was such an awesome prof to have for MATH 151! She genuinely cares for her students and makes her lectures entertaining. She uses web assign for homework and there are weekly quizzes in recitation.  If you can, get her!!! Thank you Sengupta!

I struggled to learn calculus from her because she skips steps in her lecture notes, but when I approached her about how I was struggling she was very willing to help me since I had shown her the amount of effort I have put in already. Be ready to study if you dont already know calculus!
I love this prof. randomly canceled class and hw and would send memes into class group me

Super sweet professor. She's super easy to reach out to (GroupMe groupchat), and super flexible (pushed back assignments due to engineering exams). Her lectures are great too and even those that have not seen calculus before can follow pretty easily.
Wonderful professor. Makes you feel special. Kind of like a mom. Would take her every semester if I could. Would also take her out to dinner.

Dr. Sengupta is one of the best professors out there. She truly cares for her students and goes above and beyond for their success. She was even willing to push assignments and due dates back in order to help give her students time to study for other classes midterms. She is super active in the class group me and was all around a great teacher.

Dr. Sengupta was fantastic to work with this past summer, I do NOT understand all the other reviews claiming she has issues with answering questions because she has always been more than happy to answer anything I, or other students, asked about. Her office hours are golden and the textbook is extremely resourceful for solving the homework. 10/10

Sengupta was a great prof! I did really bad in the class, but that was totally unrelated to her as a prof. She explains things really well and encourages questions in class (go to class!). She also records lectures which made it easy to look over topics I was confused about. She's very accessible outside of class and super chill.
She teaches really well, the rest is up to the student to study enough for the exams and get the grade they deserve.

Professor Sengupta is by far the best math teacher I've had here. She cares about students and makes sure that there are enough opportunities for students to reach her if they are confused about a certain topic. She is so precious and makes funny jokes during lecture too. Overall a really great lady.

Sengupta is a really good prof for MATH-152. She is really good at explaining the material, and she takes the time to go over a lot of exam-like questions which is really helpful at the moment of studying. She is also really nice and cares about her students, and usually gives extensions on homework deadlines if needed.

She is awesome. Math 152 was supposed to be a drop out class, but I got higher grades on every exam than on Math 151. She's very helpful, and you can pass if you do your homework and attend lectures. She's also super helpful and funny in office hours. Overall, 10/10. She made calc easy to understand. I always looked forward to her classes :)

I took MATH 140 with Sengupta. She is the best 140 professor out of all of them. Take her. I hate math, & the class was still really hard for me, but I did procrastinate & not start out super strong so that's on me. Take Sengupta if you need 140!!

Solid choice for MATH 152! This class has the reputation of being one of the hardest math classes at TAMU, but Sengupta is very detailed in her lectures and works numerous examples. Practice tests are exactly like the exams, so practice practice practice! She was very active on the class groupme which was pretty cool! Definitely recommend!!!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Most of these ratings are from people who either procrastinated or refused to go to office hours. Dr. Sengupta is an excellent professor who knows her stuff but will not tolerate procrastination/excuses. As long as you keep up with the homework and go to office hours if you need it, you'll definitely pass. There's also tutoring in the MLC.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: This class requires a decent amount of work as there is a good amount of homework which as well as the tests are not too easy. Showing up to class is important for the I clicker pop quiz questions which are pretty easy as long as you show up. The class is manageable, but you will have to put in work to get the grade you want.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She gives a lot of homework but it's only a small percentage of your grade so your test scores are what your grade mainly relies on. I'm a terribly test taker so this class was a bit harder for me. I even went to Tutor John and spent over 11 hours studying for the final exam and still failed. She's also not very good at answering questions in class
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Sengupta is one of the most caring professors Ive had so far. The course material is pretty simple but she explains it well and provides a fair amount of homework, typically due weekly. Theres also weekly group quizzes and tests every three weeks or so, half multiple choice and half free response. Print out the notes, DONT TRY TO HANDWRITE!!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sometimes she over-explained irrelevant information such as vocab and then rushed harder problems at the end of class. She was nice, and she can be sassy, but I found it funny. She posted the videos and notes, which helped a lot. The quizzes were done in groups, which made them easier.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sengupta was a real gem and was very good at teaching. Attendance does not matter but there are pop group quizzes and iClicker quizzes that force you to show up. The material is pretty straightforward and she provided help whenever I needed it. She frequently extended due dates and was very kind. She doesn't give a lot of time for the exams, though
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You better be able to teach yourself because Sengupta is just a terrible teacher, nice lady and I wish the best for her but cant explain something to save her life.

Dr. Sengupta is an amazing person outside of class, but she was a difficult professor. I felt that her notes did not give enough information to understand the work that I had to apply to both the homework and exams. She is also not good at replying back to emails and will sometimes never reply to emails.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Math 140 is not too hard of a class, she is a pretty good professor, and explains things pretty slowly. She makes everything accessible online, like lectures, but there are clicker questions. She hosts week in reviews to help out, but sometimes gets flustered when people ask questions. She is a very nice lady, sometimes hard to reach outside of cla
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Sengupta is one of the best math profs on campus. Math is hard for most people but her lectures were clear and she gave you all the tools needed to succeed. Always accessible during office hours as well as the TAs. Lots of homework which is expected for a college-level math but overall an A is possible if you put in the work. 100% recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She really wants her students to succeed. Lots of chances to go to office hours and hosts weekly review sessions. Also posts recordings of all the lectures which is extremely helpful if you miss class. In class quizzes were always done as a group. Sometimes she gets frustrated with questions people ask but ultimately she just wants every to pass.

The most caring and compassionate professor, she was never afraid to crack a joke and was very accommodating when it came to homework due dates. She taught relatively slow and was very understanding with all questions. The best math 140 professor on campus.

She is such a sweet lady. So many ppl complain about not being able to understand her but I think thats just an excuse for not understanding the content. You CAN understand her. She does not write the course so dont hold that to her. Math 140 is hard. She does what she can to get you a good grade. But I love her she is a sweetheart.

The class was the usual math course. lots of weekly homework, sometimes three assignments on the same week as an exam. the professor seemed irritated every time I asked for help, almost like I should already know everything. MLC was very useful for this course especially since I had a hard time gaining things from her lectures. iclicker questions
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is my professor for math 140. Math 140 is a horrible class and drop out rates are very high due to the failed design of the course. However, I am so glad I have professor Sengupta. I am horrible at math, but she has made it not only bearable, but I also have an A! She records all of her lectures so you can refer back to them when studying!

A caring professor. Will answer your questions and work with you if you seek her out. Lots of homework and lecture heavy. Attendance is important. She is caring about situations and is willing to work with students.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: one of the WORST professors at tamu. she tries to joke but they arent funny, she is terrible at explaining & hardly ever makes it through the notes. she also will tell you to ask questions but when you do she ignores you - so just dont ask, TAKE ANYONE ELSE!!! also the TA isnt helpful either! good luck to ya! gigem!
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: As a transfer this is my last basic class. I havent taken a math class since my junior year of high school and Im currently a senior. So I have questions, obviously. Professor Sengupta is the rudest professor Ive had in college hands down. She acts like answering questions is ridiculous. And the TA isnt any help either. Worst class ever.

Took summer math 140 with her. The only reason it was difficult for me was bc it was a compressed 5 week semester. I had to put in a lot of work to get an A. The things people are complaining about, like the amount of hw, are outside of her control set by the course lead. She takes time to answer questions throughout lecture, and is very nice.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: genuinely one of the worst professors Ive had. shes rude to anyone that has an issue with class or learning. She acts like answering questions in class is one of the hardest things to do and she rarely finishes notes in class. The summer class with her was absolute hell. I had to spend so much time on this class alone that I had to drop others.

fine professor i guess but kinda hard to follow in class and regularly responds to questions as if it is a problem for her to answer those questions. I wouldnt recommend taking her as there are other profs that make this class and little more tolerable and not such a pain. but if you do take her, you can pass the class and understand the work.

An angel sent from heaven. I love her! One of the best profs I've had so far. She is so sweet and communicative. She is easy to contact outside of class and will do her best to answer everyone's questions. As long as you pay attention in class and truthfully do all the homework, you should be okay.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: MATH 152 for Spring Semester. Prof Sengupta does a great job explaining each topic in the notes. She makes sure to include multiple examples. Prof S makes it easy through extensive practice. Python labs are run by your TA. Take multiple past exams as they serve as great review for each exam. Do the work assigned to be successful in this course!

Probably one of the best Math Professors I have ever had. She really hammers down a lot of the concepts and ideas as well as giving us ample opportunity to ask her questions. Do the homework, do the practice exams, and go to class and you really have no excuse for getting an A+ in the class.

Best professor I've had and I doubt there will ever be a better one... Her communication with students is amazing and she always makes sure we are understanding the lecture content. She genuinely wants the best for everyone. Her teaching methods are great and she prepares you very well for the tests/quizzes.

Dr. Sengupta was an amazing teacher for MATH 152. This is a tough class, but her notes are great. She explains things slowly to make it very digestible for students. Sometimes she would have to post pre-recorded lectures which would be 30-1hr each, but it would always help. Do previous common exams until you understand the material.

I took her class virtually and it was terrible, she has little patience and gets easily frustrated. She hardly ever covered the material necessary in class resulting with her uploading many extra lectures that you had to watch on your own time. Many kids liked her because she would joke around with them, but if you want a good teacher over jokes...

Sinjini was an absolute pleasure to have and exemplifies what it is to be an amazing professor at A&M. She is extremely well connected with her students and communicates exceptionally by being in the class groupme. She makes calc 2 easy to digest and with a little extra practice, makes it an easy A!

Dr. Sengupta was an amazing professor who made calc 2 so much easier than it seems. Although attendance isn't mandatory, attending her class will help you know everything you need to know for exams! The format of this class is similar to Calc 1: common exams, webassign homeworks, etc
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Sengupta was like our Calculus Mom. She did amazing this semester despite Texas having hurricanes and winter storms in the same weeks. She cares about each student. You do have to work for this class. Just attend lectures and take notes. Go back and study a little. Calculus 2 isn't an easy class, but Dr. Sengupta made it fun and easier for us.

Someone else also said this but she made calc 2 easier than calc 1! Her lectures are very clear, she has office hours twice a week, and as long as you do the homework you'll be fine. I was just sad she's not taking calc 3

She was a very good professor. Did many examples in class and made additional videos outside of class if you needed more examples. Made sure everyone was ready for the tests. Explained the concepts extremely well and was very nice to all her students. She somehow managed to make calc 2 easier than calc 1, which is amazing.

Very nice prof, good lecturer and was always engaged and transparent with the students; only problem was she was often behind in lectures compared to other profs in the department and so at times homework and studying felt rushed

One of the nicest profs - I had her for calc 3 and she gave super clear lectures/relatively easy exams. I wasn't the best at the material but she helped me a ton in her office hours! The homework/notes was near the same difficulty as the exams from my experience. Highly recommend her if math isn't your strongest subject!

Let me start off by saying that she is overrated. She may be caring and nice but she is not equipped to teach online, therefore, I would only take her in person. She would always cram up material the week before the exam and would take weeks grading stuff. I feel as if this class is good for procrastinators but not for people who have a study plan.

This class was extremely rushed as Sengupta would fall behind at times and post more material that we did not have time to cover in class. There was just not enough time to learn as we all had other classes. The grading also took at least 2 weeks and was a killer wait. Any material or information would always be posted late at night which sucked.

The reviews citing delayed grading/disorganization/tough expectations are true. HOWEVER, I would take Dr. Sengupta again in a heartbeat. She is truly gifted at teaching the material. Her lectures are clear. I think people who participated and engaged with the material on a weekly basis earned relatively easy A's. If you're here to learn, take Dr S!

Worst professor at A&M without a doubt. Does not care about students when they are struggling. Made one bad grade on a test and she told me that I wasnt cut out for engineering and I should switch to an easier major. She makes excuses for her personal matters, but when it comes to the students she does not care at all.

Professor Sengupta is a very caring prof, however, transitioning online has been hard for students and teachers. She fell behind on material and there was a lot of catching up to do. But if you are willing to grind, you should be fine. You can make a B if you do all the practice exams and homework, but for an A you will have to work very hard.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Sengupta is phenomenal! There is some learning on your own but if you go to office hours she'll do everything she can to help students understand. Super caring prof who wants everyone to succeed. An amazing choice for Calc 3 and if you put effort forth you will do well!

You HAVE to put in the practice to do well in calc 3. I found myself doing a lot of self teaching this semester, but Sengupta will be very helpful if you ask questions. She fell behind on material a couple times and ended up cramming the last few sections, but lectures were good. She posts extra material as well if you want more lecture problems.

I have mixed feelings about Sengupta. This course felt rushed at times and she didnt provide many examples in lecture. But shes very caring and will push homework back when were busy, but sometimes it was because we were behind, especially towards the end. Exams were alright. She definitely thrives more in person than over zoom tho.

Sengupta was fine. After the pandemic, and even before the pandemic, you can tell she is pretty serious about teaching, and is trying her best. I was fortunate enough to get an amazing TA to help me out, but overall, I'd say she can do the job of getting you a good grade if you put in enough effort.

I retook Calc I with Sengupta. Her class is very fair and she is a very kind professor. If you do your homework, go to the TA's when you need help, and do the provided practice tests, you will be very capable of making an A.

I don't know if this class is online this semester, but there is just so much rushing involved in this class. We don't get through everything in class and you have to really work hard on your own time. If it wasn't for the first test and not knowing what to expect, I could have had an A right now. Study the material after each lecture to get an A.

It's hard to find things to complain about with Sengupta. Theres a lot of homework and the tests are tough, but that's the standard for MATH 151, 152, and 251 (I've had her for all three). She's very kind, understanding, and wants to get to know you, as well as being a very solid teacher. You can't go wrong with Dr. Sengupta.
Great prof for calc 3. Cares about you and is lenient in general. Exams are pretty straightforward and everything about them is covered in class.

Genuinely cares about our success in her class. After our second exam, she sent a Zoom poll asking about how we would suggest the next exam be formatted. After taking a bit more time than usual to get exam grades back to us, she apologized profusely and was responsive to our questions in class. Rare for a calc professor:)

I love this lady so much. Shes so organized, knows exactly what shes going to teach and when. You can just tell she puts so much effort into everything she does. She really cares about you learning the material and is probably the best professor I've ever had. If you can get her, take her and as long as you put the right effort in you'll pass.

Took prof Sengupta's class right as covid hit, her in person lectures were amazing. She really worked to help take these more complex theorems and equations, and break them down into understandable bits and even give physical examples. Even after covid hit and we went online, she had great lectures and really helped make sure we were getting it.
Good professor. Explains the conceptual side well, then follows up with practical examples.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you really struggle with calculus, she is good since she goes very slow. But if you are decent at calculus, the lectures will be incredibly boring, as she teaches very slow. She got kind of rude when we moved online. If someone asked a question she thought was dumb, she made it very obvious, to the point that I felt bad for those students

Doesn't care about your time. Her lectures often went over time and she would get angry when people started packing up to leave. Type of prof who thinks her class should be your most important. Overall a good teacher if you like being taught at snail pace. She gets through half a note packet in one class and often you have to look stuff up for HW.
Dr. Semgupta is a good teacher and really nice. She posts her notes and fills them out during lecture. She does go kind of fast and the class was pretty hard.

Sengupta is quite nice and helpful. Her lectures are clear but she does go thru stuff a little fast. Encourages participation & feedback, attendance is a must. Print the notes before class or have them ready to write on a tablet. Calc 2 is hard in general but going to her office hours, wk in review, etc helped a lot. Def one of the better 152 profs

Dr. Sengupta is a great professor and always prepared us well for the common exams. Her dedication to live lectures during the COVID-19 Epidemic is a testament to how much she cares about students success.

Good professor; makes sure the class understands the material. I was going into Cal II thinking it was going to be extremely hard, but Dr. Sengupta helped me understand topics in a effective manner. Would recommend her for Cal I/II!

Sengupta is an amazing professor, you actually want to go to class because she is such a good lecturer. She is probably one of the best MATh 151 professors out there. I would've definitely done much better in her class if I didn't have to spend so much time on my ENGR 102 and CHEM 107 classes. If she is one of your options go for it.

Dr. Sengupta was an awesome professor. I really enjoyed this class and thought she made it much easier than I thought Cal 2 would be. You can tell she cares about her students and she did a great job to be prepared to teach effectively online during the coronavirus. Office hours are a great way to get help if you are struggling. Very approachable!!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a solid prof. If you're taking calc for the first time, great prof; she goes at a very good, slightly slower pace to really give you the chance to get all the info. However, if you already have a decent amount of calc knowledge from HS, she MIGHT go a little slow for you. It is by NO MEANS a boring slow, but just keep that in mind
I skipped class practically everyday, but test day and was fine. Look at her notes she takes in class and if you aren't goof at calc attendance matters, however if you are it's a blowoff.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Sengupta. She has amazing lectures and if you show up and so the work outside the class you will easily get the grade you want for the class. She is always available for students and even offers to meet with students if they no longer have her just to help her. TAKE HER!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Great teacher, posts all notes online and they make sense. Easy to get A if you do homework/practice tests.

Excellent math teacher for both Calc I and II. Anyone who has the chance to take her class should. She moves quickly during lectures but is open to questions and encourages participation from students. Challenges you to think and solve some of the problems for yourself instead of talking at you for 50+ minutes. Really cares about her students.
Dr Sengupta is a very nice woman along with being a very good teacher. I was never once confused and the rest of the class seemed to feel the same way. Made the class of 300 feel like 30.
Dr. S is great. She makes the class way easier than AP calc AB was in high school. Show up to her lectures, print out the notes, and you'll be fine.

Very good teacher, posts all lecture notes online so if you miss you aren't screwed, not too much homework and it isn't hard, easy A especially if you've already taken calculus. Funny, kind, approachable, tests are similar to practice tests. Just practice the material and you'll do perfectly fine. There's lots of help available if needed.
This class is very easy if you have taken calculus 1 before. This professor is very approachable and will answer any questions you have

Dr. Sengupta is a very nice person and her lectures are always detailed, yet clear and concise. She is very patient with her students and always does her best to explain everything to make sure there is no confusion. If you pay attention in class and do your homework, an A is pretty easy to get.

Sengupta is probably the best math prof I have had in college. She responds quickly to her email, has office hours almost every day, and gives out all kinds of different resources for you to succeed. Her lectures are easy to follow and she always does problems that will be on your homework and on your test. She genuinely wants to see you do well.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had Sengupta two semesters in a row, and both times she was a very good teacher. she cares about you succeeding if you care too, and she is not afraid to roast you. She will help you in office hours as well, and knows who you are even with a class size of 300.

If you took cal 1 in high school this class will be very easy. She teaches the class as if you have never done it before so for me so the lecture would get boring at times. I would skip when I was really tired and it was never hard to catch up she uploads all her notes so that's a huge plus. Since you take common exams you can find practice online.
AMAZING TEACHER! Do the work, office hours, and easy A!

Sengupta is a great math teacher who knows what she's talking about and is very willing to help explain any difficult concepts. There is a moderate amount of homework, but her notes are very similar to homework questions.
Amazing lecture system, saves notes from class. Good humor and can keep the class interesting.
Never went to class and relied on notes she posted online, which are really detailed and easy to follow. Final is all mc and not too bad.

Sengupta is a solid math professor. She goes slower than the other math professors which isn't my favorite teaching style, but I know some people who enjoyed it. The quizzes and programming were all group work and she was always at office hours. Definitely a good choice.

I was worried about Clac 2 but Sengupta is absolutely amazing. She explains everything clearly with steps and does example problems. Her lectures are online to refer back to later. If you want an A, go to class and do the homework (actually do it-don't just look it up). The way she explains it in class makes a huge difference. HIGHLY recommend.
She is a great professor. The way she teaches and explains things made Cal 2 as easy as I think any professor could have made it. She will also extend homework due dates if need be.

Dr. Sengupta was great. Math 152 is a notoriously hard class, but she made it as easy and understandable as possible. I am really happy I got her as a professor, and I would recommend her to anyone needing any course she teaches.

I was already solid in Calc 2 thanks to taking BC in high school, but Sengupta is a solid professor who gives clear lectures and always takes student questions both in and out of lecture. Usually exams are graded within a week. Provides her notes on eCampus. Math Lab and Recitiation were seemingly pointless, but that was not her fault as a prof.

Is very responsive to questions and tries hard to make sure all of her students understand the material. Will move homework deadlines if she feels the class doesn't understand the material enough. Her lectures are clear and precise, making the steps of the problems easy to follow.
Dr. Sengupta is a great professor. She is very easy to understand and is good at explaining topics. I even tried to get her for Math 152 but her class times didn't work with my schedule.

Dr. Sinjini is one of the better professors teaching the course. She is great at explaining the topics in an understandable way and actually cares about your grade. She is great with giving feedback and is very accessible. Would definitely take again.

Amazing teacher. Posts notes online before each lecture. Lectures can be boring if you took calculus in high school, but not unbearable. Genuinely feels like she cares. Friendly but professional in office hours. Homework can be overwhelming if you do it all at once, but otherwise fine. Tests can be tricky but aren't super difficult.

She has a small voice in a large lecture hall. She cares and will help you, but honestly my grades improved when I stopped going to class because I couldnt hear her anyways and often would fall asleep.

Excellent professor. Explains things clearly, caring, and available outside class. Accent is easy to understand, but in large classes, sit near the front so you can hear her best. Didn't use the textbook in class, but it helps to have it if you need more practice on certain problems.

I didn't struggle at all with this class because Sinjini was such a great prof. She teaches you everything you need to know for the exams and answers all of your questions during class. Take her, she's great and underrated!

Dr. Sengupta is a very good professor. She provides the notes she does in class and the week in reviews on her webpage. Overall, you will need to provide some effort to achieve your desired grade, but the class isn't too difficult.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Sengupta can sometimes go fast through her notes but she posts everything online and does a good job of explaining everything and will answer any questions you have too. There is a lot of WebAssign homework, but on her notes she gives lots of practice problems like the homework which makes it much easier.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you do not understand something, she will explain it several times in different ways until you do. She does have lots of office hours and they are very helpful especially if you get stuck on a topic. There is a lot of homework and you truly get what you put into the class. I did not take calc before and she helped me one on one.
Very kind and lakes the lectures light-hearted, posts completed notes with examples online which is a life saver! Good with answering questions.
Senupta is a solid choice for this class. Her lectures are very clear, she provides previous exams as practice, and she goes out of her way to help students. She's also hilarious.

Sengupta is probably my favorite professor I've ever had. Her lectures are extremely clear, consisting of a little bit of a topic then example problems covering it further. She gives tons of help for exams like a repository of old tests, and very clearly cares about her student's success. If you have any sort of question she won't hesitate to help.
Sengupta was a great professor. Not too difficult to follow her lectures, and all the notes are posted online.

Sengupta is a total homie! She totally deserves a higher score. She is super caring, easy to understand, funny. Does a lot of in class examples so going to lectures is recommended. Do the homework on webassign, it helps with recitation quizzes and exams. The one downside is that she will always do one more problem with 3 minutes left in class.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Solid teacher and hse actually cares about your well being
Professor Sengupta was a solid professor who always made sure that everyone was following along okay. She was thorough in her lectures and gave plenty of examples.

Dr. Sengupta is a very solid choice for a math professor. She'll make silly mistakes on examples but overall she teaches the course well. She makes the material easy to understand, and she rarely goes off on tangents. She wants you to succeed and she is friendly if you have questions. If you go to class and do the homework, you'll likely get an A.

Very nice and very caring prof. Goes through material at a good enough speed to understand. She sometimes skips some work in example problems. but very often. Start homework early because sometimes there can be a lot but too often. She posts her notes on eCampus too if you're too lazy to show up to class.

She gives easy-to follow lectures. Handwriting is clean. She answers questions in lectures. If you're looking for a stand-up comedian, go elsewhere. If you want someone who knows what they're doing and is easy to talk with, she's your prof.
reviews.ratingTags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Shes literally the sweetest, most caring professor I have ever had! She is very clear and concise in her explanations, and definitely knows what she is taking about. TAKE HER, YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT, SHE IS AMAZING!!
She's a solid lecturer, and does a great job at moving through the material at a slow enough pace for the students to understand. Would definitely recommend taking her if you can.

She sometimes skips steps during notes to get to the answer quickly but it isn't too difficult to understand. She explains everything very well and also has office hours in case you miss an exam, etc. Solid professor.

Really cares for students, I was so grateful to have such an understanding and kind professor - I highly recommend her, she will really try to help you understand the material inside and outside of class! She is a great professor and fast grader, she actually knows how to post grades on time and accurately, she also posts her notes online

Dr. Senugpta is caring, and easily accessible outside of class. Her tests are very straightforward and while her class is fast-paced, the notes are easy to follow and include examples that she lets the class work on in groups. She was fast when grading tests and made all of her homework relevant to the coursework. One of the best profs I had.

I thought she was a really good prof; she explained things really well and would go back and review things she thought we needed to see again. There's webassign every week, but doing it helps practice the material. If you put in the effort, you can do well in this class.

Overall a great prof. She really cares about her students, and makes sure to post notes and extra resources before tests. She was great about listening to her students and making sure they were well prepared before exams.

She hand writes her notes and posts them so you don't really have to go to class, but if you don't go to class you won't understand her notes. She really cares and will help you understand the material. It's an easy passing grade if you put the effort required

I didn't end up getting the grade I wanted in Dr. Sengupta's class, but I can't fault it on her teaching. She is quite a good prof. Lectures well and explains thing in a satisfactory manner, although she does tend to go fast at times.

She is awesome!! I barely came to class at all bc all her notes are super easy to understand and on ecampus. Math152 is the hardest math in TAMU from what I've heard, so it will be hard to get the grade you want no matter what. If she knows you well enough & sees that you're trying, she'll try her best to help you like how she bumped my B+ to an A.

Good professor, gives clear concise explanations and posts her lecture notes. I would highly recommend her class if you are willing to put in the work and want to actually learn the material. I used the text book to work extra problems, but you don't need it.

Sinjini was great, except that she had a very distracting home life that caused her to stop grading things halfway through the semester... but this worked out because she didn't grade my final and just gave me an A in the class. She's the OG clutch
Professor Sengupta is always willing to help in  understanding of course material. He shows  a lot of examples during lectures and posts lectures slides. She also adds extra points to exams.

Did a great job in lecture, boring at times but definitely covers everything relevant. Tests are relatively easy, paying attention in the lectures and studying the homework assignments before the exams will get you an A
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: Sengupta is an amazing professor who clearly explains the material and has a desire for her students to excel. Whenever I went to her office hours for help she would work with me and make sure that I fully understood the concept I was struggling with before I left. Would highly recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a really nice lady, and genuinely cares if you learn.  That being said, she is an extremely tough grader (she cost me my 4.0), and tends to get irritable if you ask questions she deems "stupid."  She is an excellent lecturer, and posts the lecture slides.  She doesn't do test reviews, and the tests are long for the period (avoid MWF classes)

She's a really nice person, but the class is pretty difficult. The lesson plan was done poorly so you couldn't transfer the knowledge you learn from lecture to homework and homework to exam. There's a lot a guessing work but enough exams to balance things out. Talk to her and she's normally really nice about helping students out who try.
She is a great professor but she takes forever on grading. She  pushes back homework to make sure we are not overloaded. Overall not bad but GRADING test SUCKS at.
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good lecturer. Her exams are very straightforward and actually test what she teaches in class. Gives solid partial credit. Would highly recommend for Cal 3.

Dr. Sengupta was one of the best professors I've had at A&M. I had her for math 151, 152, and 251. She truly cares about her students doing well and is always available to help outside in office hours. She goes at a good pace and pushes back any hw if need be.

Sengupta is very understanding and always willing to move the homework/edit exam content if we hadn't covered material in class. We ran behind on the curriculum and she seemed disorganized for each lecture, but this may have been because it was her first semester to teach 251. Overall great prof! Very helpful, always willing to answer questions!!
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Had her before, and she was better for those classes because this was her first time with 251. But I still liked her. Took a long time to grade tests, but willing to work with you - helps explain homework problems in office hours, and made the final optional. Really sweet lady.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great teacher for 151 and 152. Her first time teaching 251 was fall 2016 so she was kinda unorganized in her lectures. Other than that I would recommend her. Especially if you go to A plus and actually do the webassign. Her test are kinda hard but she is an easy grader and she always pushes back the HW.

I took AP Calc, but still I think she did a really good job explaining things. She was really kind and approachable, and open to questions. The homework isn't too bad, and the tests don't really have any nasty surprises. Just go over past exams well. Never used my textbook. I wanted to take her for 152 too, but she's not teaching it next semester.

Sengupta is amazing. She genuinely cares about you and wants you to succeed. Expects a fair amount from you, but isn't unreasonable. She will give points back on a hard test question or push homework due dates back usually if you just ask her to. If you're struggling, lecture and office hours are very very helpful (especially office hours!).

Learning the material is so much easier if you go to class bc she explains things really well but if you cant make it she posts all the notes online which is really nice. If you have a question on the online hmwk or a problem you couldnt work through just ask her to go over it in class and she will be more than happy to. Sengupta is a solid prof.

Her notes are all hand written which seems like a hassle but actually helps in the long run, she also posts all of her notes on eCampus. She is concerned with the well-being of her students and is very understanding of the difficulty of some sections in the class and will adjust the class and homework schedule to accommodate.

Sengupta is a very solid choice for 151, 152, 251. In 251 since there are no common exams, she was very lenient with what went on the test, often gauging her students. HW gets pushed back often and her lectures are very clear. Outside tutoring will also help (A+).
reviews.ratingTags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is her first semester teaching 251. She is one of the better math profs. She teaches almost as well as Amy Austin, but her tests are easier. 4 tests, one on each chapter. She gives a lot of homework but its a course wide homework. Its also a good study tool. She moves it back a lot if you ask nicely. 10/10 would recommend.
Very good prof. Makes a few mistakes, but they're nothing major. Cares if you learn and is willing to help by pushing back homework or the like. Would recommend.

She is very sweet and cares to see students do well. She does her best to answer all your questions and ensure you understand the concepts. She often gives extensions on homework, and she posts her notes online. Her accent is easy to understand, and genuinely cares about her students and how well they do in the class.

Great professor! I had her for the summer course  and although she rushed everything she always posted notes and encourage us to ask question. There will be a lot of HW but at the same time she offers help. Exams where easy, you just have to review the notes and it won't hurt to do previous semester exams. It also helps that she can funny at times.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great prof

LOVE her! Had her for 151&152. 152 was the first time I ever struggled with math, but she was super helpful - go to office hours! They're 4 days a week for 3 hours!!! HW will take a long time. Final is easy. Sometimes got a little flustered in lecture so you may need to clarify after class. If she sees you're confused in lecture, she'll re-explain!

Common exam class. But since its a common exam, she makes her final so easy and all multiple choice. She has a fun accent that you can understand. She tends to move back homework due dates if you go to class and ask nicely. Math 152 is hard overall, but she helps you learn it and understand it.

This is definitely not an easy A. Tests are difficult. However, if you go to class and do the homework, it is definitely possible to make an A. Her lectures are very clear and she will help you if needed. Final exam is cumulative. She takes a long time to grade tests and quizzes. Attendance not mandatory, but she does give pop quizzes.

Dr. Sengupta makes a good professor for this course. She's organized, posts notes online, and answers questions pretty well. Her accent is not hard to understand at all. Expect a fair amount of homework, and work past exams to study for the tests. If you've taken cal 1 before, this class is pretty easy and if not, it's not too bad.

First of all, Math 152 is a hard course if you haven't taken calculus before. This class is straightforward notes and then an average level test if you are prepared. Sengupta offers office hours where she will answer any doubts you may have. Definitely recommend.

I took Calculus my senior year and that is really what got me through this class. It's not easy, and requires you to work outside of class, but she is really fair. She offers 5 extra credit points on every test, PLUS there's never a question you haven't seen before. She also posts class notes online.

Calculus isn't an easy class no matter what professor you have. I loved Sengupta as a person but her class was definitely frustrating. Her lectures weren't bad but expect homework and a lot of time spent outside of class trying to learn the material. She did not curve or give extra credit. Overall this class was a very stressful.
I loved her as a person, but expect homework!! Shes not very good with time management. We ended up rushing the last couple of sections. Her final was easy though! Attendance was taken randomly

I love Dr. Sengupta. Such a cute little lady. She is a good professor and will always answer questions and clarify things during office hours. There are also week-in-reviews and other resources. Her class is difficult but her tests are so reasonable and based exactly on the things that she taught.

She posted all the notes online and worked out lots of problems in class. She definitely taught what would be on the test and prepared you well. She doesn't curve but her final was really straight forward and if you do the work you will be well prepared
Fair lecturer and teaches topics from a different angle. May help or hurt you depending on the teaching styles you have had in the past.

-ALWAYS went over lecture time so slightly annoying -flexible, pushes back homework dates if needed -slight accent, easily understandable -if youve taken calc in high school you should be fine even tho the course moves fast -answers questions in lectures -overall, very thorough and a good teacher -easy (ish) final

Dr. Sengupta is an AMAZING professor. She is very clear and thorough, and always answers questions in class. However, you need to put in a lot of work to make an A. If you go to class and take notes everyday, make sure to do all the homework, and study a little before the tests, you will be well prepared to make an A. She sets you up to do well.
Her lectures were a little long, and she always went over the time. She wasn't as bad as some other professors were. She kinda didn't always show us the easiest ways to do the harder concepts.

If you ask a question, she answers thoroughly & ensures you understand- never blows it off. Theres corresponding practice problems and tutorial videos to help w/ HW. Required max 1.5 hrs work/wk. Goes quickly in class but you can ask for help after class/office hours to clarify, and she posts notes online. Pretty easy A, esp. if you've taken CalAB

Dr. Sengupta is a fantastic professor. I would ask her questions almost everyday after class and she would always try to help and answer the questions. I can actually look back through the year and say that I have learned a lot. Definitely recommend to everybody and want to take her again for Math 152.  ( She is super nice as well!)

Lectures covered all the material that was on the test. There is homework every week for a grade but it helps to do as study material for the common exams. Sometimes went slow and got behind the course schedule but ended up barely covering everything by the end of the semester. Great job of teaching and had great test scores across her whole class.

I absolutely LOVED Dr. Sengupta. She was by far my favorite prof. of my freshmen year. She explains things extremely well. She is really good about asking questions which she answers thoroughly until the concept is understood. Class is fun and also, if you talk to her outside of class, she is super awesome and funny.  Would take her again X 100000
Dr. Sengupta is overall a good professor. I would recommend her to anyone. She's even just as good as JD Kim or Amy Austin. She's very helpful with students and cares whether you pass or not.

Am taking sinijini again because I liked her way of teaching. Go to recitation for the quiz. The tests are easy to get an A on, just do past exams to study and make sure you review your answer on the test at least twice. The class isn't curved, test averages are usually a 77.  She moves homework if she feels she doesn't cover the material well.
I love Sengupta. She's pretty chill and tends to crack jokes to lighten the mood.

She really isn't a good teacher to take if you don't already know most of calculus.  She moves extremely fast and although she'll ask for questions, she makes you not want to ask any since she looks at you as if asking, " How did you possibly get into this class?"

She speeds through calculus on some days. Some days shes slow and nice and some days she just go super fast, but she makes sure you know the essential stuff. She writes the essentials for you so copy them down if you can keep up. Otherwise shes kinda cute imo. Anyways, if you know cal, then youll be fine, youll like her. if you don't know cal sorry

Dr. Sengupta is a very intelligent and helpful professor. If you didn't take calculus in high school, expect to have some trouble keeping up. She will be there to help but you will get nowhere without practice on your own time. She also brings lots of personality and enthusiasm to the class.

Dr. Sengupta rocks. She knows what she's doing, she listens to her students (but is still firm enough to hold her own), and does a fantastic job being thorough and ensuring no student was left behind. If you want to do well in her class, she allows you every opportunity to do so -- but keep in mind that your grade is EARNED.

She's a slow grader, but willing to go over the tests, homework, and anything in general if you come in for office hours. She'll sometimes give extra credit if you show up for lecture, and she gives a lot of examples which is extremely helpful for the webassign.
Very clear on course material and nice and helpful. Tests are difficult but passable. She helps and is nice yet drags on lecture.

She goes very fast during lecture, if you zone out then you'll be lost. She is helpful in office hours and answers most questions asked in class. Occasionally she doesn't cover all concepts for the homework in lecture which makes it difficult. Also she doesn't curve, so if you don't do well on the common exams you will suffer in the class.
Gives a lot of resources to keep track of concepts, which is extremely useful since she moves rather quickly through lectures.
She is very clear cut and posts notes online for you to look over as she goes pretty fast during lectures. I would recommend going to class in order to grasp the concepts easier and STUDY ON YOUR OWN

Dr. Sengupta is very nice and helpful and an overall great professor. The only complaint I have is sometimes she talks super fast through problems and is hard to keep up with. Coupled with a slight accent, it makes lectures sometimes difficult.
Although class is not mandatory, I recommend you go. Dr. Sengupta explains concepts very well. She posts her notes and grades on ecampus, which is a plus. Overall, I felt very prepared for the exams.

Dr. Sengupta is an amazing, caring, exceptional teacher who really conveys the material well. Her lectures will help prepare you for the common exams, but you still MUST study on your own (I used webassign, past tests, and the textbook to study--but focus on past tests). Also, from what I've heard, her final was easier than those of other profs.

She goes through the material thoroughly and makes sure you are always prepared. She is very understanding and is willing to give extra time on homework if you have a test or other commitment. The homework is tedious, but her class it self is not that bad.

Her lectures are very clear and thorough. She covers almost every topic on exams. Its not essential to go to class because she posts all notes online but in lecture she will answer all questions and will help in office hours. She teaches very well and i highly recommend her.

Took this class two semester back and it was quite easy. Some things seemed hard but she would clear it up later. The Week-In-Reviews are HIGHLY important to go to. There is material she won't cover in class and will do so here also problems covered here where most likely on the test. The TA at the time was amazing and always willing to help.

The professor has a slight accent so she can be difficult to understand at times but she teaches with clarity and she is very helpful if you go to her office hours. There is a lot of homework with this class so it is very time consuming. Her tests are quite hard. You need to be sure to know the material like the back of your hand to get an A.

I personally liked Dr. Sengupta. She truly cared about her students and if you ever went to her office hours, she is more than happy to help. Her tests are a little tricky but overall she taught somewhat well.  Would recommend taking her if have a strong math background.

I am an A student and her class gave me trouble. She did not have consistent test styles, which made it difficult to study. The homework was pretty easy, the tests were just tricky and took longer than the allotted time. On top of this, she was not helpful at all. I would not recommend this professor.

Only take Sengupta if you have taken statistics before or are familiar and good at math. Thankfully I knew most of the material she covered but if I had not her way of explaining math does not seem effective. She goes through material very fast and cannot give good answers to questions. The homework is extremely easy but the tests are difficult.

The class was pretty straight to the point if you actually knew and understood what you were doing you were fine. Her exams are easy but very tricky and their is homework due online every week. Her quizzes were tough being that she timed us (2 -10 minutes). The take home assignments were not that bad. Her class isn't hard, easier prof to me.

She is a very friendly professor, and I think she truly cares about her students. She does a small review before every lecture which can take away from lecture time, so she tends to go over class time or not teach as much as she should. Overall, if you do the recommended homework and practice, you should do well on her exams.

She teaches very well and with clarity.  However, the tests are a little time consuming, meaning lots of problems in little time.  As long as you go to class, do the homework, and look at her recommended problems you'll do fine! :)
Overall, as long as you attend some week in review and do all the homework, there is no reason why you shouldn't receive an A
